components.name: Keycaps
components.description: A keycap for each of the keys given, shown as given, as ShortcutLabel draws them on the platform, for keys that are not one shortcut: a chord, a range or keys of one's own. Each key has its own keycap on every platform, macOS's too; assistive technology hears the keys separated by spaces.

components.name: ShortcutLabel
components.description: The keycaps of a shortcut, from ui.Modifiers and a ui.Key, as the platform shows one in settings or a cheat sheet: on macOS one keycap holding the menu's glyphs in the order ⌃⌥⇧⌘ (inferred; AppKit has no keycap control), on Windows 11 a keycap per key 4 DIPs apart (PowerToys's KeyVisual: ControlFillColorDefault, a 1-DIP CardStrokeColorDefault border, corners of 4), on GNOME AdwShortcutLabel's .keycap per key 6 pixels apart (currentColor at 10%, a 2-pixel inset shade, corners of 6). ui.Cmd stands for the command key of the platform drawn, so a Preview of Windows on a Mac shows Ctrl. Assistive technology hears the shortcut.

components.name: ShortcutText
components.description: The text of a shortcut as the platform's menus write it, for a menu-like row or a tooltip: ⇧⌘T on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+T on Windows 11 (WinUI's KeyboardAccelerator text, modifiers Ctrl, Alt, Windows, Shift) and Shift+Ctrl+T on GNOME (GTK's accelerator label, modifiers Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Super). ui.Cmd stands for the command key of the platform drawn, as for ShortcutLabel.
